earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct; Glottolog entry retired/merged into Ukit [umi]; no description of Seru located

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2022. Change Request 2022-014: adopted merge [szd] Seru into [umi] Ukit (effective 2023-01-20). Dallas: SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Administrative merge form; rationale (p. 2) quotes Hammarstrom: the Sru were a fraction of the Ukit and 'every word' of Bailey's 1901 wordlist was understood by Ukit 'as belonging to their own language' (De Rozario 1901:332). Sources cited: De Rozario 1963 [1901] and Glottolog only.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A comprehensive classification. PhD diss., University of Hawai'i at Manoa. Sec. 2.4.3.5 'Sru Dayak', pp. 122-123.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States the total evidence base: Bailey's 1901 list of 170 items is 'the only linguistic material that was ever collected for this now-extinct language' and 'The detailed phonetics of the language are impossible to extract from the wordlist' (p. 123). Uses the list to classify Sru as a Punan language (shared lexicon; retention of *-b-; final high-vowel breaking *-u > -aw).

sources.citation: Rensch, Calvin R. 2012. Melanau and the Languages of Central Sarawak. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012-011. 100 pp.
sources.note: Not a Seru source: no Seru/Sru/Bailey mention; and no stress statement for any language in it (per the ukit1237 audit).

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1913. The Languages of Borneo. Sarawak Museum Journal 1(4): 1-196.
sources.note: Not a Seru source: grep for Seru/Sru finds no column or mention (only Howell & Bailey's Sea Dayak dictionary). Checked because it is the main Ukit reference.

Kuching: Borneo Literature Bureau. Originally in The Sarawak Gazette, 1901.

sources.note: The only linguistic material ever collected for Seru (170-word list). Worth opening only to check whether the list carries any accent marks or a remark on pronunciation; Smith 2017 judges detailed phonetics unrecoverable from it.
